s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dysphagia with significant weight loss and respiratory symptoms
salient_findings: Progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids
Weight loss of more than 100 lbs
Episodes of food getting stuck in the throat
Hoarseness and tongue paralysis with atrophy
key_facts: 60 pack-year history of tobacco use
Progressive dysphagia over a three-month period
Weight loss of more than 100 lbs
Night sweats
Hoarseness
Tongue paralysis with atrophy on cranial nerve testing
Cachexia and exaggerated cervical lordosis
Normal lymph nodes
Productive cough without fever, chest pain, or hemoptysis
Large confluent anterior cervical osteophytes on CT
Bilateral noncalcified pulmonary nodules at lung apices
Enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes on CT
Diffuse innumerable pulmonary nodules predominantly in lung bases on CT

shortlist.label: Hypopharyngeal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive dysphagia, significant weight loss, and hoarseness

shortlist.label: Oropharyngeal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Tongue paralysis, atrophy, and cranial nerve testing abnormalities

shortlist.label: Esophageal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Extrinsic compression of upper esophagus on EGD and dysphagia

shortlist.label: Pancoast tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral noncalcified pulmonary nodules and weight loss

shortlist.label: Mediastinal lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes on CT and night sweats

raw.rationale: The patient's progressive dysphagia, weight loss, night sweats, hoarseness, and tongue paralysis with atrophy are consistent with hypopharyngeal cancer. The presence of a large retropharyngeal mass partially obstructing the airway on flexible laryngoscopy and extrinsic compression of the upper esophagus on EGD also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Oropharyngeal cancer
rejected.why: While possible, the symptoms and findings are more consistent with hypopharyngeal involvement

rejected.label: Esophageal cancer
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and findings, such as hoarseness and tongue paralysis, are not typical for esophageal cancer

rejected.label: Pancoast tumor
rejected.why: The patient's findings, such as the large retropharyngeal mass and extrinsic compression of the upper esophagus, are not consistent with a Pancoast tumor, which typically presents with shoulder pain and Horner's syndrome

rejected.label: Mediastinal lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and findings, such as the large retropharyngeal mass and extrinsic compression of the upper esophagus, are not typical for mediastinal lymphoma
